resources.string: Exports the /root workspace and drydock config (system layers are replayed per recipe version and not included); the file lands in Downloads/Drydock/drydock-env-export.tar.gz; it contains ~/.drydock/env.sh — environment variables you stored (including keys) go into the export.\nRestore merges into the current environment: new files are written directly, same-name files with different content are asked one by one (overwrite all / skip all); if the environment is not deployed it is deployed first.

Selected %1$s (%2$s).

The backup will be merged into the current environment; existing files with the same name will ask to overwrite or skip.
⚠ ~/.drydock/env.sh from the backup enters the environment — keys stored in it come along.

Restore rewrites files inside the environment and cannot be undone; consider closing running sessions first. If the Linux environment is not deployed it will be deployed automatically first (about 1 minute).
Both the import package and the current environment have this file, with different content:
%1$d more name conflicts after this one
✗ Rejected as a whole, environment untouched: %1$s
✗ Deploy failed, restore aborted (network/storage issue; retry)
✓ Rolled back: %1$s → %2$s (changes made after the upgrade were carried back by the reverse migration)
User files migrated: %1$d · excluded: %2$d (caches/sockets etc.) · user copy kept on conflicts: %3$d\nManual apt packages: %4$s\nManual npm packages: %5$s
One-click reinstall (manual packages are not reinstalled by upgrade, D33):

Upgrade side-deploys: download and unpack into a side directory → verify sha256 (mismatch aborts the switch) → atomic directory-rename switch; the old version is kept for rollback (peak disk usage about 2× rootfs).
/root user files are migrated per blacklist (excluding .l2s*/.npm/.cache/AndroidDownload/*.sock); on conflicts with the new template the user copy always wins; manual apt/npm packages are not reinstalled automatically — the report gives the reinstall command.
Upgrade and rollback stop all sessions and rebuild them from the registry afterwards (running commands and shell contents are not kept).
Update sources: built-in version pin + local update index (files/rootfs-updates.json).

This will upgrade to %1$s. All sessions will be stopped (rebuilt automatically afterwards; running commands are not kept); /root user files and the workspace migrate to the new version; manual apt/npm packages need reinstalling per the report.

This will roll back to %1$s. All sessions will be stopped (rebuilt automatically afterwards); /root files created or modified after the upgrade are carried back to the old version by the reverse migration and are not lost.
